learn.headline: Plugin compresses long AI sessions so they run on smaller context windows.
learn.reason: Shows context compression, a core cost and context idea you're learning next.

card.headline: Popular new add-on helps coding assistants keep very long chats going
card.gist: A new add-on sits between coding assistants, like Claude Code, and the AI model. It folds older chat into summaries, so one session can last much longer.
card.picture: Think of rolling up old daily rows into a monthly summary table. The raw rows can be reloaded when you need exact details. Here, the AI itself decides which old messages to roll up.
card.why_you: Long Claude Code sessions slowly fill the AI's working memory, and quality can drop. Knowing how to shrink old history helps you design agents and explain them in interviews.
card.remember: Summarize old chat, but keep the exact details possible to restore.
card.term_meaning: Replacing older parts of an AI conversation with shorter summaries, so it fits the model's memory limit.
card.say_it: In long agent sessions, I summarize older turns instead of simply cutting them off.
card.follow_up_why: Because every token costs money, and past the window limit the session degrades or fails.
card.reality_check: The 5x token-savings claim appears in the project's own description. The repo also lists benchmarks it calls independent; I have not checked them.
card.try_it: In a long Claude Code session, type /context to see what fills its memory.
